blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
SLA design, at senior level, is a customer experience decision dressed up as an operations decision. The windows you promise, the recovery paths you commit to, and the compensation you offer when something goes wrong collectively shape how customers feel about your brand — often more than the product itself. A good experience on a failed delivery can build loyalty; a bad experience on a successful one can destroy it.

What matters at this level is alignment. Marketing cannot promise windows that operations cannot hold. Operations cannot quietly extend windows that marketing has sold. Finance cannot squeeze the SLA until the recovery paths become hollow. The three functions must agree on a single, defendable promise — and accept the cost of keeping it.

It is the honesty of the SLA, not its tightness, that builds customer trust. Companies that promise less than they can deliver tend to keep customers for years. Companies that promise more tend to lose them, one disappointed Tuesday at a time.

items.q: According to the text, an SLA is best understood as…
options: a legal document owned by finance
a marketing commitment with no cost
a customer experience decision framed as an operations one
items.why: "a customer experience decision dressed up as an operations decision."

items.q: What does the text say builds customer trust?
items.why: "It is the honesty of the SLA, not its tightness, that builds customer trust."

items.q: What must the three functions agree on?
items.why: "The three functions must agree on a single, defendable promise."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with which statement?
options: Marketing and operations must promise the same thing.
The tighter the SLA you advertise, the more customers trust you.
A failed delivery can still build loyalty if handled well.
items.why: Inferência: o texto argumenta que é a honestidade, não o aperto, que gera confiança — prometer mais afasta clientes.

items.q: The phrase "one disappointed Tuesday at a time" suggests that…
options: customers are lost gradually through repeated small failures
one large incident destroys a brand instantly
delivery problems only happen on Tuesdays
items.why: Inferência: a perda de clientes é cumulativa, feita de decepções pequenas e repetidas, não de um único evento.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Sophie conduzindo a reunião de alinhamento. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Thank you all for coming. Before anyone opens a spreadsheet, let me be clear about what this review is not: it is not a negotiation to see how tight a window we can advertise. It is an attempt to agree on one promise all three of us can stand behind on a bad day.

Here is where we are. Marketing has been selling a next-day window. Operations tells me we hold that window about seventy per cent of the time. And when we miss it, the recovery path is hollow — a form, an apology, and a voucher nobody redeems. So we advertise a promise we keep two days out of three, and handle the third day badly. That is the worst of both worlds.

What I want us to leave with today is not a tighter number. It is an honest one. If operations can defend a two-day window ninety-eight per cent of the time, I would rather sell that, with real compensation behind it — something that restores trust when we slip.

Finance, I know the instinct is to squeeze this. But a promise we cannot keep costs far more in lost loyalty than the compensation ever will. Let us design the experience, not just the number.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: How does Sophie define what this review is NOT?
options: A meeting to replace the marketing team
A review of the product itself
A negotiation to advertise the tightest possible window
A budget-cutting exercise led by finance
items.why: "it is not a negotiation to see how tight a window we can advertise."

items.q: What is the current problem with the next-day window?
options: It is held only about seventy per cent of the time
It is never advertised to customers
items.why: "we hold that window about seventy per cent of the time."

items.q: Why does Sophie call the current recovery path "hollow"?
options: It is too expensive to maintain
It is a form, an apology and a voucher nobody redeems
items.why: "a form, an apology, and a voucher nobody redeems."

items.q: What does Sophie mean by "the worst of both worlds"?
options: The two-day window is too slow to advertise
They over-promise AND handle failures poorly
The company loses money on every delivery
Marketing and operations refuse to speak
items.why: Inferência: eles prometem o que só cumprem 2 em 3 dias e ainda tratam mal o terceiro dia — falham nas duas pontas.

items.q: What can be inferred about Sophie's message to finance?
options: She agrees the SLA should be squeezed to save money
She thinks compensation should be removed entirely
She believes lost loyalty is more expensive than compensation
She wants finance excluded from the decision
items.why: Inferência: "a promise we cannot keep costs far more in lost loyalty than the compensation ever will" — ela contesta o instinto de apertar.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "When we miss the window, the recovery path must restore trust." A recovery path is…
options: the process for putting things right after a failure
the marketing campaign after a launch
the route the delivery driver takes
the refund line on the invoice
items.why: Recovery path = caminho de recuperação: o que a empresa faz para reparar a experiência quando algo falha.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "If finance keeps trying to ___ the SLA, the recovery paths will become meaningless."
items.why: To squeeze = apertar/espremer: reduzir custo até esvaziar a promessa.

items.q: "A voucher nobody redeems makes the compensation hollow." Hollow here means…
items.why: Hollow = oco: parece uma compensação, mas não entrega valor real.

items.q: Choose the correct term: "We need a promise the whole business can stand behind — a truly ___ SLA."
items.why: Defendable = defensável: uma promessa que a empresa consegue sustentar mesmo num dia ruim.

items.q: "It is the honesty of the SLA, not its tightness, that keeps customers." Tightness refers to…
options: how tightly the contract is written legally
how ambitious or narrow the promised window is
how limited the customer base is
how strict the finance budget is
items.why: Tightness = aperto: quão agressiva/estreita é a janela prometida — o oposto de uma promessa folgada.

blocks.instruction: Expressões que aparecem em reuniões de alinhamento de SLA. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "Finance still has to sign off on the compensation budget." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar formalmente, dar o aval final.

items.q: "We will roll out the two-day window market by market." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = implementar de forma progressiva.

items.q: "Operations pushed back on the next-day promise." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, questionar — sem necessariamente rejeitar de vez.

items.q: "Marketing sold the window but never followed through with operations." They…
options: failed to see the commitment through
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim aquilo que foi combinado.

items.q: "A voucher nobody redeems will not move the needle on loyalty." This means it will…
items.why: Move the needle = mexer o ponteiro, fazer diferença perceptível.
